docs.title: Welcome
docs.text:
Troy Reynolds Datasheet as part of Fill-A-Bot for Team 201

Individual Subsystem: Liquid Amount Sensing

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
This datasheet documents the design and development of my individual Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem for the Fill-A-Bot project. The subsystem is responsible for measuring the amount of liquid in the system and providing this information to the rest of the embedded system.

The subsystem uses a load cell to measure weight. Because a load cell produces a very small differential voltage, a load-cell ADC/amplifier is used to amplify and digitize the signal before it is processed by the PIC18F57Q43 microcontroller.

docs.title: Project Summary
docs.text:
The Fill-A-Bot is a team embedded-systems project consisting of multiple subsystems that work together to control and monitor the movement and dispensing of liquid.

My portion of the project is the Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem. Its purpose is to measure the amount of liquid present so that the system can monitor changes in liquid quantity and provide measurement data to the main controller.

The subsystem is based around a load cell, load-cell ADC/amplifier, and PIC18F57Q43 microcontroller.

docs.title: My Contribution
docs.text:
My individual contribution is the design and implementation of the Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem. This includes selecting the sensing components, designing the electrical connections, interfacing the sensor electronics with the PIC18F57Q43, and documenting the subsystem.

The major components selected for the subsystem are a Soldered Electronics 555026 1 kg load cell and a SparkFun SEN-13879 HX711 load-cell ADC/amplifier.

The following sections document the development of my subsystem:

  • Block Diagram
  • Component Selection
  • Bill of Materials
  • Schematic
  • Power Budget

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The individual block diagram documents the electrical design of the Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem for Fill-A-Bot. The subsystem uses an external 1 kg load cell to measure the combined weight of the container and liquid. The small differential signal produced by the load cell is measured by a Nuvoton NAU7802KGI 24-bit sigma-delta ADC with a programmable gain amplifier.

A Microchip PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano processes the weight measurement and interfaces with the Fill-A-Bot main controller using a four-wire direct digital interface. Two command inputs, C1 and C0, select one of four weight presets, while two status outputs, S1 and S0, report the current state of the Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem.

The subsystem also includes local 5 V power regulation, a load-cell connector, ADC interface circuitry, a tare/zero pushbutton, status LED, GPIO expansion, and test points.

docs.title: Individual Block Diagram
docs.text: Figure 1: Individual block diagram for the Fill-A-Bot Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem.

docs.title: Power
docs.text:
The subsystem accepts a 9–12 V DC input through a 2-position screw-terminal connector. The input passes through a 500 mA fuse and fuse holder before reaching an LM7805CT linear voltage regulator.

The LM7805CT converts the input voltage to a regulated 5 V supply for the subsystem. A 0.33 µF capacitor is connected at the regulator input and a 0.1 µF capacitor is connected at the regulator output to help stabilize the regulator.

A local 5 V selection jumper connects the locally regulated supply to the +5V_BOARD rail used by the subsystem electronics.

The simplified power path shown in the block diagram is:

9–12 V Input → 500 mA Fuse/Holder → LM7805CT → +5 V Regulated

docs.title: Liquid Amount Sensing
docs.text:
The subsystem uses an external Soldered Electronics 555026 / 100382 1 kg load cell to measure the combined weight of the container and liquid.

The load cell uses four electrical connections:

  • E+ — Positive bridge excitation
  • E− — Negative bridge excitation
  • A+ — Positive differential output
  • A− — Negative differential output

The external load cell connects to the sensor PCB through an On Shore Technology OSTVN04A150 4-position load-cell connector.

The E+ and E− connections provide excitation for the load-cell bridge. The A+ and A− connections form the differential analog measurement pair.

The A+ and A− signals are routed through the analog input circuitry to the NAU7802KGI. Two 47 Ω series resistors and a 0.1 µF capacitor provide filtering for the low-level differential signal before analog-to-digital conversion.

The block diagram simplifies the external load-cell connection as a single functional connection labeled:

E+, E−, A+, A−

docs.title: NAU7802 ADC Interface
docs.text:
The Nuvoton NAU7802KGI is a 24-bit sigma-delta ADC with a programmable gain amplifier. It amplifies and converts the small differential voltage produced by the load cell into digital measurement data that can be processed by the PIC18F57Q43.

The load-cell differential measurement signals connect to the NAU7802 through:

  • VIN1P — Positive differential ADC input
  • VIN1N — Negative differential ADC input

The NAU7802 connects locally to the Curiosity Nano using three digital signals:

NAU7802 Signal PIC18F57Q43 Pin Purpose SDIO RB2 Digital data and ADC configuration SCLK RB1 Digital clock DRDY RC0 Indicates when a new ADC conversion is ready

The SDIO and SCLK lines use 4.7 kΩ pull-up resistors.

This ADC interface is local to the Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem and is separate from the direct digital communication used between the Fill-A-Bot subsystem boards.

docs.title: Team Communication
docs.text:
The Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem communicates with the Fill-A-Bot main controller using four direct digital HIGH/LOW signals rather than UART or I2C.

Two signals, C1 and C0, are inputs from the main controller and form a two-bit weight command. Two signals, S1 and S0, are outputs from the Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem and form a two-bit weight status.

The 8-position team connector uses the following connections:

Connector Pin Signal PIC Pin Direction Purpose Pin 1 C1 RA3 Input Weight-command bit 1 Pin 2 C0 RA4 Input Weight-command bit 0 Pin 3 S1 RE2 Output Weight-status bit 1 Pin 4 S0 RC7 Output Weight-status bit 0 Pin 5 NC — — Unused Pin 6 NC — — Unused Pin 7 NC — — Unused Pin 8 GND GND — Common ground between subsystem boards

docs.title: Weight Command
docs.text:
C1 and C0 allow the main controller to select one of four weight presets.

C1 C0 Command 00 Preset 1 01 Preset 2 10 Preset 3 11 Preset 4

C1 and C0 connect directly to PIC pins RA3 and RA4.

The command path is:

Main Controller → C1/C0 → RA3/RA4 → PIC18F57Q43

docs.title: Weight Status
docs.text:
S1 and S0 allow the Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem to report its current state to the main controller.

S1 S0 Status 00 Not ready 01 Below target 10 Target reached 11 Error

S1 and S0 are generated by PIC pins RE2 and RC7.

The S1 and S0 outputs will be initialized LOW by the subsystem software.

The status path is:

PIC18F57Q43 → RE2/RC7 → S1/S0 → Main Controller

The team connector does not carry subsystem power. Pins 1 through 4 are used for direct digital communication, Pins 5 through 7 are unused, and Pin 8 provides the common ground connection between the subsystem and main controller.

docs.title: Tare / Zero Input
docs.text:
A momentary pushbutton is connected to PIC pin RA0 and is used as the TARE/ZERO input.

The input uses a 10 kΩ pull-up resistor. When the button is not pressed, the input is held HIGH. When the button is pressed, RA0 is connected to ground and becomes LOW.

The PIC can detect the button press and establish the current load-cell measurement as the zero or tare reference. This allows the weight of the empty container to be removed from subsequent liquid measurements.

A 1 µF capacitor is included to help filter and debounce the pushbutton signal.

docs.title: Status LED
docs.text:
A green status LED is controlled by PIC pin RC1 through a 1.2 kΩ current-limiting resistor.

The LED provides a visual indication that can be controlled by software to show subsystem status, measurement activity, tare completion, or debugging information.

docs.title: GPIO Expansion
docs.text:
A 6-pin expansion header provides four additional general-purpose I/O connections labeled GPIO1 through GPIO4.

The expansion header also provides +5V_BOARD and GND for connection to additional external hardware if required.

docs.title: Debugging and Test Points
docs.text:
Five test points are included on the subsystem PCB to provide convenient access to important power and ADC-related signals during subsystem testing and verification.

The status LED, tare/zero pushbutton, GPIO expansion header, and test points provide additional hardware access for testing and debugging without changing the normal operation of the Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem.

docs.title: Design Summary
docs.text:
The Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem measures liquid weight using an external 1 kg load cell and the NAU7802 ADC and processes the measurement with the PIC18F57Q43.

The measurement path is:

External Load Cell → Load-Cell Connector → Analog Input Circuitry → NAU7802 → PIC18F57Q43

The command path is:

Main Controller → C1/C0 → RA3/RA4 → PIC18F57Q43

The status path is:

PIC18F57Q43 → RE2/RC7 → S1/S0 → Main Controller

The power path is:

9–12 V Input → 500 mA Fuse → LM7805CT → +5V_LOCAL → JP2 → +5V_BOARD

The four-wire digital interface allows the main controller to select one of four weight presets and allows the Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem to report whether it is not ready, below the target, at the target, or in an error state.

docs.title: Component Selection
docs.text:
Individual Subsystem: Liquid Amount Sensing

The Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem measures the amount of liquid in the Fill-A-Bot using an external load cell. The small differential signal from the load cell must be amplified and converted into digital data before it can be processed by the PIC18F57Q43 microcontroller. The following sections compare potential load cells and load-cell ADC/amplifier solutions for this subsystem.

docs.title: Load Cell Selection
docs.text:
Table 1: Load cell component selection

Load Cell / Weight Sensor

Solution Pros Cons Option 1Soldered Electronics 555026 / 1003821 kg Load Cell$15.96/eachLink to product * 1 kg maximum load is appropriate for the liquid container* Operates from 5 V to 10 V* 2 ±0.1 mV/V output sensitivity* Wheatstone bridge design works with a high-resolution load-cell ADC* Detailed electrical characteristics are available * More expensive than the Adafruit option* Requires an ADC/amplifier to measure the small output signal* Requires calibration Option 2Adafruit Industries 45401 kgf Load Cell$3.95/eachLink to product * 1 kg measurement range is appropriate for the project* Lowest-cost load cell of the three options* Compact load-cell design * Requires an external ADC/amplifier* Requires calibration before accurate measurements can be made* Less detailed electrical documentation Option 3Seeed Technology 3149900000-500 g Load Cell$17.00/eachLink to product * Designed for electronic weighing applications* Recommended 5 V excitation matches the subsystem supply* 0.5 ±0.1 mV/V output sensitivity* ±0.05% full-scale nonlinearity * Maximum capacity is only 500 g* Container plus liquid could exceed the 500 g limit* Most expensive load-cell option* Requires an external ADC/amplifier

Choice: Option 1: Soldered Electronics 555026 / 100382 1 kg Load Cell

Rationale: The Soldered Electronics 555026 was selected because its 1 kg maximum load provides an appropriate measurement range for the liquid container used in the Fill-A-Bot. The sensor operates from a 5 V to 10 V excitation supply and produces a 2 ±0.1 mV/V differential output from its Wheatstone bridge. This allows the load cell to operate from the subsystem's regulated 5 V supply and interface with a high-resolution bridge-sensor ADC. Its documented electrical characteristics, 1 kg measurement range, and compatibility with the selected NAU7802 load-cell ADC make it well suited for the Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem.

The load cell is external to the Liquid Amount Sensing PCB and connects to the board through the 4-position load-cell connector using E+, E−, A+, and A−.

docs.title: Load Cell ADC / Amplifier Selection
docs.text:
Table 2: Load cell ADC/amplifier component selection

Load Cell ADC / Amplifier

Solution Pros Cons Option 1SparkFun Electronics SEN-13879HX711 Load Cell Amplifier$11.50/eachLink to product * 24-bit ADC designed for weigh scales and bridge sensors* Built-in low-noise programmable gain amplifier* Selectable gain of 32, 64, or 128* Operates from 2.6 V to 5.5 V* Complete breakout board simplifies prototyping * More expensive than a bare ADC IC* Maximum standard sample rate is 80 SPS* Breakout-board implementation is not appropriate for direct integration into the final subsystem PCB* Requires software calibration Option 2Nuvoton Technology NAU7802KGI24-bit Load Cell ADC$2.26/eachLink to product * 24-bit sigma-delta ADC designed for bridge and strain-gauge sensors* Programmable gain from 1 to 128* Digital SDIO/SCLK interface to the microcontroller* Operates from 2.7 V to 5.5 V* Through-hole 16-PDIP package* Integrates directly onto the PCB* Significantly less expensive than the HX711 module * Bare IC requires additional support circuitry* More software configuration is required* Requires configuration before measurements can be taken Option 3Texas Instruments ADS1232IPWR24-bit Bridge Sensor ADC$8.50/eachLink to product * 24-bit ADC specifically designed for bridge sensors and weigh scales* Low-noise programmable gain amplifier* Selectable gains of 1, 2, 64, and 128* Two differential input channels* Operates from 2.7 V to 5.3 V * Surface-mount 24-TSSOP package is more difficult to prototype* Requires additional external support components* More complex PCB layout* More expensive than the NAU7802

Choice: Option 2: Nuvoton Technology NAU7802KGI

Rationale: The Nuvoton Technology NAU7802KGI was selected because it combines a 24-bit sigma-delta ADC with a programmable gain amplifier designed for precision bridge and strain-gauge measurements. Its programmable gain allows the very small differential output of the load cell to be amplified before analog-to-digital conversion. The device operates from 2.7 V to 5.5 V, making it compatible with the subsystem's regulated 5 V supply.

The NAU7802KGI is available in a 16-PDIP through-hole package, allowing the ADC to be integrated directly onto the subsystem PCB without using a daughter board. At approximately $2.26 per device, it is also significantly less expensive than the HX711 breakout board and ADS1232 option. These characteristics make the NAU7802KGI the best fit for the final Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem.

docs.title: Microcontroller Configuration
docs.text:
The Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem uses a Microchip PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano for processing, local control, and communication with the Fill-A-Bot main controller.

The following PIC18F57Q43 pins are used by the final subsystem design:

Figure 1: Final MCC pin configuration for the PIC18F57Q43 used in the Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem.

PIC Pin Configuration Connected Function RB2 Digital output initially; direction controlled in software NAU7802 SDIO RB1 Digital output NAU7802 SCLK RC0 Digital input NAU7802 DRDY RA3 Digital input C1 weight-command bit 1 RA4 Digital input C0 weight-command bit 0 RE2 Digital output S1 weight-status bit 1 RC7 Digital output S0 weight-status bit 0 RA0 Digital input TARE/ZERO pushbutton RC1 Digital output Status LED RD0 GPIO GPIO1 expansion RD1 GPIO GPIO2 expansion RD2 GPIO GPIO3 expansion RD3 GPIO GPIO4 expansion

The NAU7802 interface is local to the Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem. SDIO provides bidirectional ADC data and configuration, SCLK provides the digital clock, and DRDY indicates when a new conversion is available.

RA3 and RA4 receive the two command bits from the main controller, while RE2 and RC7 return the two subsystem status bits. RA0 is used for the tare/zero input and RC1 controls the status LED.

Unused Curiosity Nano pins are not required for normal subsystem operation.

docs.title: Team Interface
docs.text:
The Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem communicates with the Fill-A-Bot main controller using a four-wire direct digital interface.

C1 and C0 are two command inputs used to select one of four weight presets. They connect directly to PIC pins RA3 and RA4.

C1 C0 Command 00 Preset 1 01 Preset 2 10 Preset 3 11 Preset 4

S1 and S0 are two status outputs used to report the current state of the Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem. S1 is generated by PIC pin RE2 and S0 is generated by PIC pin RC7.

S1 S0 Status 00 Not ready 01 Below target 10 Target reached 11 Error

The S1 and S0 outputs will be initialized LOW by the subsystem software.

J1 Pins 5 through 7 are unused, and Pin 8 provides the common ground connection between the Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem and the main controller.

The team connector does not carry subsystem power.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The following Bill of Materials lists the components used in the Fill-A-Bot Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem. The subsystem uses an external 1 kg load cell and a NAU7802KGI 24-bit ADC to measure liquid weight, a PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano for processing and control, and a four-wire direct digital interface for communication with the main controller.

The team interface uses two command inputs, C1 and C0, to select one of four weight presets and two status outputs, S1 and S0, to report the current state of the Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem.

The Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem communicates with the Fill-A-Bot main controller through J1 using four direct digital signals.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
The 1 kg load cell is external to the Liquid Amount Sensing PCB and connects to the board through the OSTVN04A150 load-cell connector using E+, E−, A+, and A−.

The NAU7802KGI is mounted directly on the subsystem PCB rather than using a separate ADC daughter board.

The team interface does not carry subsystem power. J1 Pins 1 through 4 are used for the C1, C0, S1, and S0 direct digital signals, Pins 5 through 7 are unused, and Pin 8 provides the common ground connection between the Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem and the main controller.

The subsystem power path is:

9–12 V Input → 500 mA Fuse → LM7805CT → +5V_LOCAL → JP2 → +5V_BOARD

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem measures the amount of liquid dispensed by the Fill-A-Bot using an external 1 kg load cell. The load cell produces a small differential analog voltage that is filtered and measured by a Nuvoton NAU7802KGI 24-bit sigma-delta ADC with a programmable gain amplifier.

A Microchip PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano processes the digital weight measurement, controls the tare/zero and status functions, and communicates with the Fill-A-Bot main controller using a four-wire direct digital interface consisting of two weight-command inputs, C1 and C0, and two weight-status outputs, S1 and S0.

The subsystem also contains its own 5 V power regulation, input protection, load-cell interface, ADC support circuitry, team connector, GPIO expansion header, status LED, tare/zero pushbutton, and test points.

docs.title: Power Regulation
docs.text:
The subsystem accepts a 9–12 V DC input through J3, a Dinkle EK508V-02P 2-position screw-terminal connector.

The incoming supply passes through F1, a 500 mA fuse, before reaching the LM7805CT linear voltage regulator.

The LM7805CT converts the 9–12 V input into a regulated 5 V supply.

The regulator support components include:

  • C1 = 0.33 µF, 25 V on the regulator input
  • C2 = 0.1 µF, 25 V on the regulator output
  • JP2 for connecting the locally regulated +5V_LOCAL rail to +5V_BOARD

The +5V_BOARD rail supplies the load-cell interface, NAU7802 circuitry, Curiosity Nano, and supporting components.

The power path is:

9–12 V Input → 500 mA Fuse → LM7805CT → +5V_LOCAL → JP2 → +5V_BOARD

docs.title: Load Cell Interface
docs.text:
The subsystem uses an external Soldered Electronics 555026 / 100382 1 kg load cell.

The external load cell connects to the PCB through an On Shore Technology OSTVN04A150 4-position screw-terminal connector.

The four load-cell connections are:

Signal Purpose E+ Positive bridge excitation E− Negative bridge excitation A+ Positive differential measurement output A− Negative differential measurement output

E+ is connected to +5V_BOARD and E− is connected to ground.

A+ and A− carry the small differential measurement signal produced by the load cell.

docs.title: Analog Input Filtering
docs.text:
The differential load-cell output is filtered before entering the NAU7802.

The input network consists of:

  • R1 = 47 Ω, 0.25 W
  • R2 = 47 Ω, 0.25 W
  • C3 = 0.1 µF, 25 V

R1 and R2 are placed in series with the two differential load-cell signal lines. C3 is connected across the differential input.

This network helps reduce high-frequency noise before the signal is amplified and converted by the NAU7802.

docs.title: NAU7802 Load-Cell ADC
docs.text:
The Nuvoton NAU7802KGI is a 24-bit sigma-delta analog-to-digital converter with a programmable gain amplifier.

The NAU7802 is used because the differential output from the load cell is very small and requires both amplification and high-resolution analog-to-digital conversion.

The primary load-cell inputs are:

  • VIN1P — Positive differential input
  • VIN1N — Negative differential input

Additional support circuitry includes:

  • C4 = 0.1 µF, 25 V
  • C5 = 1 µF, 25 V
  • C6 = 1 µF, 25 V
  • R5 = 4.7 kΩ, 0.25 W
  • R6 = 4.7 kΩ, 0.25 W

C4 provides filtering for the ADC reference circuitry.

C5 and C6 provide local supply filtering and decoupling for the ADC circuitry.

R5 and R6 provide pull-up resistance for the NAU7802 digital interface.

docs.title: NAU7802 to Microcontroller Interface
docs.text:
The NAU7802 communicates locally with the PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano using SDIO, SCLK, and DRDY.

NAU7802 Signal PIC18F57Q43 Pin Purpose SDIO RB2 Bidirectional digital data and ADC configuration SCLK RB1 Digital clock DRDY RC0 Indicates that a new ADC conversion is ready

The PIC uses these signals to configure the NAU7802 and retrieve converted load-cell measurements.

This interface is local to the Liquid Amount Sensing PCB and is separate from the direct digital communication used between the Fill-A-Bot subsystem boards.

docs.title: Team Communication
docs.text:
J1 is the 8-position team connector used to interface the Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem with the Fill-A-Bot main controller.

The subsystem uses four direct digital HIGH/LOW signals rather than UART or I2C between boards. Two signals, C1 and C0, are command inputs from the main controller. Two signals, S1 and S0, are status outputs from the Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem.

J1 Pin Signal PIC Pin Direction Purpose 1 C1 RA3 Input Weight-command bit 1 2 C0 RA4 Input Weight-command bit 0 3 S1 RE2 Output Weight-status bit 1 4 S0 RC7 Output Weight-status bit 0 5 NC — — Not connected 6 NC — — Not connected 7 NC — — Not connected 8 GND GND — Common ground between subsystem boards

C1 and C0 form the two-bit weight-command input and connect directly to PIC pins RA3 and RA4.

The weight-command encoding is:

C1 C0 Command 00 Preset 1 01 Preset 2 10 Preset 3 11 Preset 4

S1 and S0 form the two-bit weight-status output from the Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem and are generated by PIC pins RE2 and RC7.

The weight-status encoding is:

S1 S0 Status 00 Not ready 01 Below target 10 Target reached 11 Error

The S1 and S0 outputs will be initialized LOW by the subsystem software.

The team connector does not distribute subsystem power. Pins 1 through 4 carry the four digital communication signals, Pins 5 through 7 are unused, and Pin 8 provides the common ground connection.

docs.title: Tare / Zero Circuit
docs.text:
SW1 is a momentary pushbutton used to tare or zero the scale.

The tare/zero circuit is connected to PIC pin RA0.

The circuit includes:

  • SW1 = Omron B3F-1020
  • R4 = 10 kΩ, 0.25 W pull-up resistor
  • C7 = 1 µF, 25 V debounce/filter capacitor

When the button is not pressed, R4 holds RA0 HIGH.

When SW1 is pressed, RA0 is pulled to ground and becomes LOW.

The software can detect this state and store the current load-cell measurement as the zero reference. This allows the weight of the empty container to be removed from subsequent liquid measurements.

docs.title: Status LED
docs.text:
LED1 is a green status/debug LED controlled by PIC pin RC1.

The LED circuit consists of:

  • R3 = 1.2 kΩ, 0.25 W current-limiting resistor
  • LED1 = Kingbright WP7113LZGCK green LED

When RC1 is driven HIGH, current flows through R3 and LED1 to ground, turning the LED on.

The LED can be used by software to indicate subsystem status, measurement activity, tare completion, or debugging information.

docs.title: Curiosity Nano Supply Filtering
docs.text:
C8 is a 0.1 µF, 25 V bypass capacitor connected to the Curiosity Nano supply.

The capacitor helps reduce power-supply noise near the microcontroller.

docs.title: GPIO Expansion
docs.text:
J4 is a 6-position GPIO expansion header.

The header provides:

  • GPIO1
  • GPIO2
  • GPIO3
  • GPIO4
  • +5V_BOARD
  • GND

These connections provide access to additional PIC18F57Q43 I/O if future expansion or additional testing is required.

docs.title: Test Points
docs.text:
Five test points are included in the design to provide access to important signals during testing and debugging.

The test points provide convenient locations for measuring power, ground, ADC-related signals, and DRDY without modifying the normal subsystem wiring.

docs.title: Design Summary
docs.text:
The Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem converts the mechanical force applied to the external 1 kg load cell into a digital weight measurement.

The measurement signal path is:

External Load Cell → Load-Cell Connector → Analog Input Filter → NAU7802 24-bit ADC/PGA → PIC18F57Q43

The weight-command path is:

Main Controller → C1/C0 → RA3/RA4 → PIC18F57Q43

The weight-status path is:

PIC18F57Q43 → RE2/RC7 → S1/S0 → Main Controller

The power path is:

9–12 V Input → 500 mA Fuse → LM7805CT → +5V_LOCAL → JP2 → +5V_BOARD

The resulting design provides the Fill-A-Bot with a dedicated subsystem for measuring liquid weight, selecting one of four commanded weight presets, zeroing the container weight, monitoring fill progress, and reporting the current weight status to the main controller.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A power budget was created for the Fill-A-Bot Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem to estimate the current and power required by the components operating from the regulated 5 V supply.

The analysis includes the PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano, NAU7802KGI load-cell ADC, external 1 kg load cell, status LED, tare/zero circuit, NAU7802 digital pull-up resistors, and Curiosity Nano external-power overhead.

A 25% design margin was added to the estimated operating current to provide additional capacity for component variation and operating conditions. The resulting design requirement was compared with the 500 mA fuse used to protect the subsystem.

The LM7805CT linear regulator was also evaluated at both the minimum 9 V input and maximum 12 V input to estimate regulator power dissipation.

docs.title: Power Budget
docs.text: Figure 1: Power budget for the Fill-A-Bot Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem.

docs.title: Current and Power Analysis
docs.text:
The estimated operating current of the subsystem is 71.79 mA at 5 V.

This corresponds to an estimated 5 V load power of:

P = V × I

P = 5 V × 0.07179 A = 0.35895 W

Therefore, the estimated subsystem load is approximately 358.95 mW.

A 25% design margin was added to the estimated operating current:

Design Margin = 71.79 mA × 0.25 = 17.95 mA

The resulting design current requirement is:

Design Requirement = 71.79 mA + 17.95 mA = 89.74 mA

docs.title: Fuse Capacity
docs.text:
The subsystem uses a 500 mA fuse on the power input.

The remaining current margin after including the 25% design margin is:

Remaining Margin = 500 mA - 89.74 mA

Remaining Margin = 410.26 mA

The estimated design requirement therefore remains well below the 500 mA fuse rating.

docs.title: LM7805 Thermal Analysis
docs.text:
Because the LM7805CT is a linear voltage regulator, the voltage difference between its input and 5 V output is dissipated as heat.

Regulator power dissipation was estimated using:

P_D = (V_IN - V_OUT) × I

For the thermal analysis, the design current was rounded to 0.09 A.

docs.title: 9 V Input
docs.text:
At the minimum 9 V input:

P_D = (9 V - 5 V) × 0.09 A

P_D = 0.36 W

docs.title: 12 V Input
docs.text:
At the maximum 12 V input:

P_D = (12 V - 5 V) × 0.09 A

P_D = 0.63 W

The 12 V input condition produces the greatest estimated regulator dissipation and therefore represents the worst-case thermal condition evaluated in the power budget.

docs.title: Conclusions
docs.text:
The Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem has an estimated operating current of 71.79 mA and an estimated load power of 358.95 mW at 5 V.

After applying a 25% design margin, the required current increases to approximately 89.74 mA.

This is substantially below the 500 mA fuse limit, leaving approximately 410.26 mA of current margin.

The LM7805CT is expected to dissipate approximately 0.36 W at a 9 V input and 0.63 W at a 12 V input using the rounded 90 mA design current. The 12 V input therefore represents the highest thermal load considered in this analysis.

Based on the calculated current requirement, the selected power system provides sufficient electrical capacity for the Liquid Amount Sensing subsystem. The regulator thermal performance should also be verified during hardware testing, particularly when operating from the maximum 12 V input.
